newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak drug maker names Nomura GDR manager.
newsitem.headline: Slovak drug maker names Nomura GDR manager.

text.p: London-based Nomura International Plc is to lead manage a 231 million crown GDR issue of Slovakia's largest drug producer Slovakofarma a.s., the company said on Friday.
"We have chosen Nomura to become the global coordinator and bookrunner of the (GDR) issue," Tibor Velky of Slovakofarma's capital investment department told Reuters.
He said the issue should be completed by the end of this year, but declined to provide any further information.
"It is all in the preparatory stage, we are working on the issue but it is still subject to approval by our shareholders," Velky said.
The company expects the annual shareholders' meeting on May 15 to approve an equity increase through the GDR issue.
Velky would not say where the GDR's will be traded or disclose whether the shares will have voting rights.
The company's basic capital currently stands at 1.523 billion crowns.
Slovakofarma, currently the most expensive Slovak share on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) has been suffering from low liquidity on the bourse over the last few months.
It traded only 15 shares on the BSE unlisted market on Wednesday, closing up 48 crowns, at 4,251.
The share price has been gradually but consistently falling from February's 5,200 crown high after soaring from around 2,800 crowns at the beginning of this year.

Slovakofarma said in February it expected an after-tax profit of around 500 million crowns for 1996, compared with a 481.2 million crown net profit in 1995. Slovakofarma officials said the company planned to pay a dividend of "around" 200 crowns per share compared with 250 crowns on 1995 profits.
